findings.title: Task 8 model test expects pew pew untargeted at round start; Part i starts it targeted on Shields
findings.claim: The Weapons panel test asserts `w.pew` toMatchObject `{ shots: 2, target: -1 }` at round start. Part i's systemsFor starts pew pew with `pewLock: Room.Shields, pewTargeted: crew && laser !== null`. The panel maps `target: sys.pewTargeted ? sys.pewLock : -1`, so it reads 1 (SHLD), not -1. The test cannot pass.
findings.evidence: plan L1845 (`expect(w.pew).toMatchObject({ shots: 2, target: -1 })`), L1909 (`target: sys.pewTargeted ? sys.pewLock : -1`); Part i plan L2530 (`pewLock: Room.Shields, pewTargeted: crew && laser !== null`) and Decision 17 L119 ('Pew pew starts full and targeted on Shields, like the beam'). `shots: 2` needs a crew laser (barrelShots returns 0 without one, Part i L2643), so whenever shots is 2, pewTargeted is true.
findings.why: Task 8 Step 6 fails at its first run, and the executor has to guess whether the test or the model is wrong.
findings.fix: Expect `target: Room.Shields` (import Room) and `ready: true` at round start. Or set `sys.pewTargeted = false` before the assertion and keep -1.

findings.title: Widening aimWeapon to 'pew' breaks FlightStation's prop type (tsc)
findings.claim: Task 8 widens `ContactView.aimWeapon` to `'pew' | 'laser' | 'torpedo' | null`. DuelUi passes `duel.contact?.aimWeapon ?? null` to FlightStation, whose `aim` prop is its own local `type Weapon = 'laser' | 'torpedo'`. `npx tsc -b` fails with TS2322. FlightStation.tsx is not in Task 8's Files or its git add, and the plan says only TargetingLine needs nothing.
findings.evidence: plan L2014 (contactModel `aimWeapon` widened), L2015, L2221 ('The widened aimWeapon type flows through unchanged'), L1783 (Files list, no FlightStation), L2236 (git add); src/renderer/src/ui/duel/DuelUi.tsx:45 (`<FlightStation … aim={duel.contact?.aimWeapon ?? null} />`); src/renderer/src/ui/duel/FlightStation.tsx:22 (`type Weapon = 'laser' | 'torpedo'`), :27 (`aim?: Weapon | null`).
findings.why: Task 8 Step 10's `npx tsc -b` (and every later task's) fails.
findings.fix: Add FlightStation.tsx to Task 8. Either narrow at the call site (`aim={duel.contact?.aimWeapon === 'pew' ? null : duel.contact?.aimWeapon ?? null}`; pew pew has no Flight card, Decision 14) or widen FlightStation's local type. Stage the file in the commit.

findings.title: Task 9 torpedo fog test moves the wrong missile pool entry
findings.claim: The test assumes `missiles` is indexed by owner and moves `t.missiles[1]`. `placeMissile` puts the missile in the first free pool entry, which is missiles[0] on a fresh state. The test therefore moves a free entry. The enemy torpedo stays at r/2, `seen.missile` stays true, and the next assertion fails. The plan itself defers this to a 'check the test's assumptions' step.
findings.evidence: plan L2300-2305 (`placeMissile(t, 1, …)`, then `t.missiles[1]!.x = own.x + r * 2;`, then `expect(v.seen.missile).toBe(false)`), L2339-2341 ('TacticalState.missiles is indexed by owner slot … the third case relies on that'); src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/state.ts:227 (`missiles: [emptyMissile(), emptyMissile(), …]`), :247-251 (`missileOf(state, i) ?? state.missiles.find((e) => !e.active)`).
findings.why: Task 9 Step 9 fails. The check-at-execution bullet is a known-false assumption.
findings.fix: Use the returned entry: `const m = placeMissile(t, 1, {...}); …; m.x = own.x + r * 2;`. Delete the 'check the test's assumptions' bullets at L2339-2341.

findings.title: Task 11 'creates' the spike report with a literal template, overwriting Part i's report
findings.claim: Part i Task 1 creates the same report and Task 12 fills it with the sim measurements, the gate and band table and the determinism lines. Part i's skipped balance gates point at that table in their it.skip comments. Part i says Part ii adds feel and screenshots to that same file. Part ii's Task 11 says 'Create' and gives a whole-file template, with 'Everything else is literal'. That template has no gate table and no list of the pre-existing tests that Tasks 7 to 9 tell the executor to record 'in the report'. The file table also says 'create (T8)'.
findings.evidence: plan L107 (`create (T8)`), L2635 ('Create: docs/superpowers/research/2026-11-18-engineering-spike.md'), L2737 ('Everything else is literal'), L2739-2796 (the template), L1598, L2020, L2228, L2548 ('say so / list each one in the report'); Part i plan L51 (the it.skip comment cites the report's gate table), L130 (Decision 19: 'Part ii adds feel and screenshots to the same report file'), L138, L169, L221-239 (Sim measurements, Gates and bands, Determinism sections), L3370.
findings.why: Following Task 11 as written deletes Part i's gate and fallout record, the evidence the owner needs to judge the spike. The 'list it in the report' instructions in Tasks 7 to 9 have nowhere to land.
findings.fix: Make Task 11 Step 4 a Modify. Keep Part i's sections. Append 'Part ii: what was built', 'App smoke and screenshots', 'Tests updated by Part ii' (from Tasks 7 to 9), 'Feel' and 'Known limits'. Fill 'Numbers' from Part i's measurement lines. Fix the file table to 'modify (T11)'.

findings.title: Task 10's measurement script duplicates Part i's, with a different workload
findings.claim: Part i already creates `scripts/engineering-spike-measure.ts` and runs it at 53 and at 54 (a Hound snapshot length, then a 3600-tick scripted Cutter duel). Part ii adds a second script, `scripts/spike/engineering-measure.ts`, that times idle Hound rounds over 5 seeds. The report would get two different 'tick cost' figures.
findings.why: It's redundant code under `scripts/` (type-checked by tsconfig.web.json), and the report's numbers would disagree.
findings.fix: Drop Task 10 Steps 1-2 and the script. Quote Part i's two measurement lines in the report. If an idle-Hound figure is really wanted, say why and label it separately from Part i's.

findings.title: New WeaponsStation calls optional ConsoleInput members without `?.` (certain TS2722), left conditional
findings.claim: Task 8 makes `pewLock?` and `weaponPower?` optional on ConsoleInput. `consoleActions` is annotated `ConsoleInput`, so `actions.console.pewLock(-1)` and `actions.console.weaponPower(slot, ±1)` in the rewritten WeaponsStation are 'possibly undefined' invocations. The plan only says 'if tsc reports them … call them with ?.'.
findings.evidence: plan L1943-1944 (optional members), L1980-1981, L2129 (`actions.console.pewLock(-1)`), L2149 (`actions.console.weaponPower(slot, 1)`), L2219 ('If tsc reports them possibly undefined…'); src/renderer/src/ui/actions.ts:49 (`const consoleActions: ConsoleInput = {`), :73 (`console: consoleActions`).
findings.why: The error is certain, not maybe. A check left to execution is a defect under this review's rules.
findings.fix: Write `actions.console.pewLock?.(-1)` and `actions.console.weaponPower?.(slot, 1)` / `(slot, -1)` in the Step 9 code, and delete the conditional note.

findings.title: The fog hides the round-start enemy, so existing tests break; the plan's fix recipe is open-ended and partly unworkable
findings.claim: Ships spawn on SPAWN_RADIUS 2000 and the round-start sensor range is 900, so the enemy is unseen from the first frame. Existing tests that click or draw the enemy at its spawn will fail. For example, contactScene expects 'ENEMY SHIP' after a click at the enemy's spawn position, and with `seen: false` contactModel returns 'CONTACT LOST'. Step 9 runs only 8 files and says 'fix the test'. Its second recipe ('raise the crew's Sensors bars') tops out at 2800, which may not reach a spawn up to about 4000 away. Failures in other files first show up in Task 10's full suite, which has no fix instruction.
findings.evidence: plan L2532 (`ships: fx.kill || !fogView.seen.enemy ? [0] : [0, 1]`), L2539, L2545, L2548; src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/tuning.ts:34 (`SPAWN_RADIUS = 2000`); Part i plan L3039 (`SENSOR_RANGE_BY_BARS = [300, 900, 1400, 2000, 2800]`); tests/contactScene.test.ts:53, :59-68 (click at `enemyOnScreen()`, expects title 'ENEMY SHIP').
findings.why: This is the risky path the review asked about (Q8). An executor in Task 10 meets unplanned failures with no rule for them.
findings.fix: In Task 9, grep the scene and UI tests that need a drawn or clickable enemy at round start (contactScene and any others that read enemy marks, arcs or the contact window). Give one recipe: move `t.ships[1]` within 900 of the crew ship before the first draw. Drop the 'raise Sensors' option. Repeat the rule in Task 10 Step 3.

findings.title: Small unstated HUD deviations from spec §6, and overlapping markers in non-point rooms
findings.claim: (a) Spec §6 puts the free coolant under the reactor column. The plan prints it in a header line, 'REACTOR x/10   COOLANT y/8'. (b) The spec's heat bar turns red near HEAT_MAX. The plan colours it by state only (hot while overdriven, blinking while failed, main otherwise). (c) In a non-point room, fireTileOf returns the breach-site tile, so a fire and a breach there draw two markers and two labels on the same tile.
findings.evidence: spec L206-208; plan L882, L944; plan L1120 and L1124 (both at `centre(fireTileOf(d, r))` and `centre(der.siteTile[s])`); Part i plan L1672-1677 (fireTileOf returns siteTile for non-point rooms).
findings.why: Clarity is one of the spike's three questions (spec Questions §2). Overlapping labels are unreadable.
findings.fix: State (a) and (b) as Decisions, or implement them (a FREE pip row under the PWR column; heat tinted hot above e.g. 75 % of heatMax). For (c), offset the breach label by half a tile when a fire marker shares its tile.
